correctness.rationale: With A high opponents earlier in the tie order and B later, the two ranks are 1+A and i+B. Their quadratic payoff difference has degree at most two; its Walsh constant is (N²+2Ni−N−4i+2)/8, singleton coefficients are −i/4 on earlier indices and (N+i−1)/4 on later ones, and pair coefficients are ±1/4 for pairs on the same side and zero otherwise. For each coordinate set U the gradients give the equal-coordinate line in the edge coefficient block, so subtracting its mean gives the residual. The only nonsingleton residuals are (N+i+j−1)²/32 per pair and 1/8 per triple. The pair sum before division by 32 is C(N,2)(N−1)²+2(N−1)² sum(i)+(N−2) sum(i²)+(sum(i))². In the total norm, writing k=i−1 and m=N−1, the numerator of the sum of singleton-coefficient squares is mN²+m²k−mk²; the quadratic terms sum to 2 C(N,3)/16. These sums and the constant coefficients yield exactly the stated T and H. For affine increments 1 the edge mean is (N−1)/2 and each singleton has magnitude 1/2, with opposing signs in each pair, giving H/T=1/N. The quadratic witness differs by the stated factorized excess; it ties at seven and is strict for all N>=8. My independent exact vertex-Laplacian replay /workspace/branches/audit_priority.py solved the normal equations directly from rank-sorted profiles (no edge Walsh coefficient computation), matched both energies for N=2 through 9 including 1919/2192 at N=8, and reproduced the seven-agent witness 53454277/62354880>6/7. For 2<=N<=6 it formed Q=H−T/N by polarization, verified its all-ones kernel vector and positive Schur pivots of the complementary principal minor (zero form at N=2), hence PSD on the whole space of increments. These checks and the analytic proof establish the exact threshold only for the stated uniform two-level complete-conflict model; there is no nonlinear optimum claim.
